_comment: RESEARCH LEADS for the Israel layer. Not yet facts.
Every row here was found via public sources on 2026-07-26 and carries the URL
it came from. Every row is `verification: "unverified"`, which means the
scoring engine ignores it and the UI renders it as 'not yet checked'.
That is deliberate. A kosher claim is not like a piste-length claim: a family
that travels somewhere on the strength of it and finds nothing has had their
holiday damaged. Web search is good enough to find candidates and bad enough
that it should never be the last word. Restaurants close, hotels change hands,
and a rabbi moves on without anyone updating a directory page.
TO PROMOTE A ROW TO `verified`: open its sourceUrl, confirm the place still
exists and still holds the certification claimed, then set verification and
put your name in curatedBy. Budget about 30 minutes for the whole file. That
half hour is what turns this from a resort database into the product.
DISTANCES ARE NOT HAND-ENTERED. Each entry carries a city location; the ETL
derives distance to each ski area geometrically. Coordinates below are
CITY-CENTRE approximations, which is the right resolution for the question
actually being asked ('is this in the village or two hours away?').

chabadCentres.name: The Rohr Chabad Jewish Community Center
chabadCentres.note: Nearest Chabad to the Bulgarian resorts. No Chabad presence found in Bansko or Borovets themselves — Sofia is the reference point, and it is a substantial drive, not a walk.

chabadCentres.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Georgia
chabadCentres.note: Reported to run Shabbat and holiday meals for travellers and a dairy kitchen in the mornings. Gudauri is up the Georgian Military Highway from here — verify current road transfer time seasonally, it is weather-dependent.

chabadCentres.name: Chabad of Milan
chabadCentres.note: Gateway city rather than a resort service. Address not captured — look it up before publishing.

kosherFood.name: My Kosher Hotel
kosherFood.note: THE most significant find for Italy. Canazei sits inside Val di Fassa, which is already in our dataset (78.1 km, Dolomiti Superski) — so this is kosher accommodation ON a resort we rank, not in a distant gateway city. If any single row in this file is worth verifying first, it is this one.

kosherFood.name: Mendi's
claimedFeatures: reported open daily noon to midnight
kosherFood.note: Tbilisi, not Gudauri. Relevant to arrival and departure days rather than the ski week.

kosherFood.name: King David
kosherFood.note: Certification level was not stated in the source. Do not render any kashrut claim for this entry until confirmed directly.

kosherFood.name: Savoia Resort Bardonecchia (seasonal kosher programme)
claimedFeatures: runs as a programme, not year-round
kosherFood.note: Seasonal programmes appear and vanish year to year. Re-check every autumn; never carry one forward on last season's evidence.

_gaps: No kosher provision found IN Bansko, Borovets, Pamporovo or Gudauri themselves — only in the gateway cities. If that holds after verification it is a real finding worth stating plainly on those resort pages, not a hole to leave blank.
Hebrew-speaking ski schools: not researched. Ask the ski schools directly; it is not published anywhere reliable.
Shabbat-workable lodging (non-electronic room entry, Shabbat lifts) needs contacting properties one by one. No shortcut exists.
Israeli school-holiday dates (Hanukkah, Passover, winter break) still need loading as a first-class date filter.
